L573: #### Maximal semisimple image
L574: We finish this subsection with an observation on the maximal semisimple image of the algebra $\Bbbk\Op_{n}$ where $\Bbbk$ is a field. Let $D_{n}$ be the subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(\Op_{n})$ with the same set of objects but the morphisms are only morphisms of the form $C(f_{Y,X})$ where $f_{Y,X}\in\OF_{n}$. Note that if $f_{W,Z},f_{Y,X}\in\OF_{n}$ then $\widetilde{Y}=Y$ (since $n\in Y$) and if $Z=Y$ then $C(f_{W,Z})\cdot C(f_{Y,X})=C(f_{W,X})$ where $f_{W,X}\in\OF_{n}$.
L575: Therefore, $D_{n}$ is indeed a subcategory (without zero morphisms) of $\mathcal{C}(\Op_{n})$. Moreover, every morphism $C(f_{Y,X})$ in $D_{n}$ has an inverse $C(f_{X,Y})$ so $D_{n}$ is a groupoid. Note also that the identity morphisms $C(e_{X})$ (for $X\subseteq[n]$ with $n\in X$) are the only endomorphisms in $D_{n}$.

L583: Denote by $R$ the subvector space of $\Bbbk_{0}\mathcal{C}(\Op_{n})$ spanned by all the morphisms of the form $C(f_{Y,X})$ where $f_{Y,X}\notin\OF_{n}$. First note that according to cite75†5.14 if $f_{W,Z},f_{Y,X}\notin\OF_{n}$ then
L584: 
L585:  | $$C(f_{W,Z})\cdot C(f_{Y,X})=0.$$  |
L586: Moreover, if $f_{Y,X}\notin\OF_{n}$ and $f_{W,Z}\in\OF_{n}$ are such that $C(f_{W,Z})\cdot C(f_{Y,X})\neq 0$ then $f_{W,Z}f_{Y,X}\notin\OF_{n}$ according to cite76†5.11 (and the dual holds if $C(f_{Y,X})\cdot C(f_{W,Z})\neq 0$). Both facts together imply that $R$ is a nilpotent ideal (of nilpotency degree $2$). Since every non-zero morphism of $\mathcal{C}(\Op_{n})$ is either in $R$ or in $D_{n}$ it is clear that $\Bbbk_{0}\mathcal{C}(\Op_{n})/R\simeq\Bbbk D_{n}$.
